_why_this_exists_before_the_review_does: AUT-PROP-006. This record is written as the seat's FIRST act, so a seat that dies leaves evidence that it looked rather than nothing at all. It is EMPTY and says so: publish_bar.clause_1_hardening_converged REFUSES any round with an open record at the commit it is grading, because an unfinished look must never be counted as a clean one.
central_claim: The published FET-fusion -> impaired-ATM -> compensatory-ATR-dependency hypothesis has weak and largely absent computational support when tested against public data for EMC: EMC tumours show no proliferation-independent DDR transcriptional signature (part B, GENERIC_ONLY / WEAK), the CRISPR dependency readout is saturated and cannot discriminate even against a matched sarcoma comparator (part C), and ATR-inhibitor sensitivity fails 3 of 4 pre-registered mechanism tests (part D); the structural precondition argument and the wet-lab ask survive, and no EMC-specific ATR vulnerability is claimed anywhere.

blockers.summary: The fourth of the four part-D bars is called 'fixed before the numbers' (SS5, line 623) and the four tests 'pre-registered' (headline line 99; SS5 line 618), but the producing module's own comment records that this bar was written BECAUSE of a prior run's numbers - and quotes the very numbers the paper still prints. The multiplier chosen with those values visible is what decides the headline count '1 of 4'.
blockers.evidence: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py at the pin, lines 2918-2924, verbatim: '# THE SECOND SPECIFICITY AXIS, and the one the fixed grading actually turns on. / # `atri_specific` above only asks "is this predictor about ATR INHIBITORS rather than about / # drugs in general". It does NOT ask "is this predictor about the MECHANISM rather than about / # PROLIFERATION" - and on run 30857647907 that gap mattered: replication-stress expression / # correlated with ATRi sensitivity at rho -0.164 while the plain proliferation control / # correlated at -0.171, i.e. very slightly MORE.' The bar it introduces is line 2935: `srec["beats_the_proliferation_control"] = bool(abs(rho) > abs(prolif_rho) * 1.15)`. Those two numbers are exactly what SS5 reports today (artifact specificity block: expr::replication_stress mean_rho_across_ATR_inhibitors -0.1637; expr::proliferation_MYC -0.1711). LOAD-BEARING: 1.15 x 0.1711 = 0.19677, and the one passing row (dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1, mean rho +0.2123) clears it by 0.0155; any multiplier >= 1.25 makes the pass fail and the count '0 of 4'. SS1's separate defence - 'None of the three has been changed since it was written, which is checkable in the module's git history' - is TRUE (I verified `len(ctrl_up) <= 1`, the `> 0.2` elevated cut and `DEPENDENT_THRESHOLD = -0.5` byte-identical at d4c623634, 19cc109c6, f45d966df, 1b5f85385, dc8621870, ad87aa4c7, 11d5de12d and the pin) but cannot carry SS5's weight: the module's FIRST commit (d4c623634, 2026-08-05) already contains this comment and four others citing runs 30856488704 / 30857647907 / 30858567419 / 30859156946 / 30859974432, so the history holds no pre-numbers version of the file and 'unchanged since written' does not imply 'written before the numbers'.
blockers.fix: Stop calling all four bars pre-registered. Say which three were fixed before the numbers (direction, |rho| >= 0.15, non-DDR drug specificity) and state plainly that the fourth - beat the proliferation control by 1.15x - was added after run 30857647907 showed replication-stress at rho -0.164 against a proliferation control at -0.171, citing the module comment. Add that the 1.15 multiplier was therefore chosen with those values visible, that its effect on the failing row is conservative, and that the one passing test clears it by 0.0155. Change 'Of four pre-registered mechanism tests, one passes' (line 99) and '1 of 4 pre-registered tests passes' (line 618) accordingly, and drop the SS1 sentence that offers the git history as verification of 'fixed before the numbers' - it verifies 'unchanged since first commit' and nothing more.

blockers.summary: SS3.4 and SS6.1 give irreconcilable accounts of what part B bounds. SS3.4 says the two nulls are 'consistency between two underpowered reads, not a demonstration that a DDR signal is absent'; SS6.1 says 'What part B bounds is real and is the whole of it: EMC tumours carry no proliferation-independent DDR signature, on two series.' A reader cannot act on both, and the arithmetic that settles it is one division of numbers the artifact already carries - the same MDE SS3.4 says was never computed.
blockers.evidence: Paper lines 538-540 against line 782. emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_b_emc_tumour_signature.per_platform[*].contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma_PROLIFERATION_ADJUSTED carries delta, t and df per concept, so SE = |delta|/|t| and MDE(80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05) = (t_.975 + t_.80) * SE. On the proliferation-adjusted contrast - the one the verdict rests on, since `ddr_concepts_elevated_after_proliferation_adjustment` is [] - every DDR concept on BOTH series is powered against the paper's own 0.2 'elevated' cut. GSE4303-GPL3290 (10 EMC vs 6): DNA_damage_checkpoint {"t": 2.378, "df": 12.7, "delta_a_minus_b": 0.0735} -> SE 0.0309, 95% CI +/-0.067, MDE 0.094; S_phase_E2F {"t": 3.602, "delta_a_minus_b": 0.1282} -> SE 0.0356, MDE 0.110; ATM_signalling_DSB_repair {"t": -1.574, "delta_a_minus_b": -0.0701} -> SE 0.0445, MDE 0.135; replication_stress MDE 0.144; stalled_fork_response MDE 0.153; ATR_CHK1_activity MDE 0.186. GSE24369-GPL6244 (6 EMC vs 29): MDE 0.045-0.118 on all six. Every value is below 0.2. (On the RAW contrast three concepts sit marginally above: ATR_CHK1 0.212, stalled fork 0.232, S-phase 0.212 - but the raw contrast is not what the null rests on.) So 'underpowered' is asserted against no criterion and is false against the criterion the paper itself uses.
blockers.fix: Compute the MDE once and make both sections say the same thing. Replace SS3.4's sentence with the quantified version - e.g. 'Part B's nulls are at n = 10 and n = 6 EMC tumours. Against the fixed 0.2 cut the proliferation-adjusted read has >=80% power on every DDR concept on both series (minimum detectable effect 0.045-0.186 in within-sample SD units, derived as SE = |delta|/|t| from the committed contrast blocks); effects below about 0.1 SD units are not excluded, and on the RAW contrast three concepts are marginal at 0.21-0.23.' Then let SS6.1's bound stand with that effect-size qualifier attached ('no proliferation-independent DDR concept exceeds 0.2, with 80% power to have seen one'), rather than as an unqualified claim of absence.

p1s.summary: The dependency-modality null SS5 names as missing is computable at $0 from the committed inputs cache, and running it SUPPORTS the passing row rather than undermining it. Leaving it unrun leaves the paper's one positive weaker than its own evidence.
p1s.evidence: SS5: 'no dependency-modality null was run. ... The null that would settle it is a pan-essential score: RPL5 (-2.744) or PLK1 (-2.715), both already computed in part C's per-gene block, and correlated against these drugs nowhere.' Both are in emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#part_c.gene_effect_by_line (1,178 lines each), and the drug residuals are in #part_d.gdsc_residual_ln_ic50_by_drug. Spearman on the same line intersections the module uses (my code reproduces every published rho and n exactly - e.g. dependency/azd6738 +0.2520 n=597, ATM-expression/ve-822 -0.1583 n=656): RPL5 azd6738 +0.0370 / ve-822 +0.0365, mean +0.037; PLK1 -0.0109 / +0.0260, mean +0.008; ATM gene effect (near-neutral control) +0.0448 / +0.0450, mean +0.045. Applying the paper's own four bars, none reaches |rho| >= 0.15, none is atri_specific, none beats 0.1968. So 'a strong dependency score of any kind predicts a drug-specific residual' is refuted on the committed data.
p1s.fix: Run the two correlations in the module (they need no fetch), print them beside the passing row, and change 'correlated against these drugs nowhere' to the result: a pan-essential dependency score does not predict the ATR-inhibitor residual (RPL5 rho +0.037, PLK1 +0.008, against +0.212 for the ATR axis), so the passing test is not explained by dependency-score magnitude.

p1s.summary: The passing row is described as agreement 'at MODULE level rather than at target level' and as 'two instruments agreeing about the same three-gene module, not about ATR', but the per-gene decomposition of the composite - from the same committed cache - shows the correlation is carried by ATR and its obligate partner ATRIP, with CHEK1 contributing essentially nothing.
p1s.evidence: Headline line 99 area and SS5. Spearman of each single-gene CRISPR effect against the same drug residuals, from emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#part_c.gene_effect_by_line and #part_d.gdsc_residual_ln_ic50_by_drug, on the same n = 597 / 565 line sets: ATR alone rho +0.290 / +0.204 (mean +0.247); ATRIP alone +0.304 / +0.220 (mean +0.262); CHEK1 alone +0.043 / +0.015 (mean +0.029); the three-gene composite +0.252 / +0.173 (mean +0.212); WEE1 alone +0.095 / +0.098 (mean +0.097). The composite is diluted by CHEK1, not carried by it, so the two instruments are agreeing about ATR/ATRIP, not about the module.
p1s.fix: Print the per-gene decomposition and replace the module-level framing with what it shows: the CRISPR-vs-drug agreement is carried by ATR (+0.247) and ATRIP (+0.262) and not by CHEK1 (+0.029). Keep the separate and still-correct point that this says nothing about EMC and that no bar here separates ATR from a neighbouring target on the DRUG side.

p1s.summary: The 2,500-column random background is the normaliser for EVERY expression predictor in part D, not just for the held-out FET signature, and the paper attributes the subspace limitation only to the signature. SS5 also describes the load-bearing ATM predictor as a raw log2(TPM+1) mean, which is not what the module computes.
p1s.evidence: Paper line 736-739 raises the subspace limit for the signature alone ('The paper reproduced the circularity half of that design note and dropped this half'), and SS5 defines the ATM row as 'a log2(TPM+1) mean over the Reactome double-strand-break-response set'. The module at the pin, D2: line 2702 `bg_cols = rng.sample(others, min(2500, len(others)))`; then `mu = bg.mean(axis=1)`, `sd = bg.std(axis=1)`; then for every concept line 2714 `s = (df[cols].mean(axis=1) - mu) / sd`. The artifact records emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_d_drug_response_correlation.expression_scores_meta.n_background_columns_for_centering: 2500 against #expression_file_choice.n_total_columns_in_file: 19193. So expr::ATM_signalling_DSB_repair (the load-bearing row) and expr::proliferation_MYC (the control the passing row is measured against) are per-line z-scores against a seeded random 2,500-gene sample of a 19,193-gene matrix, not raw set means.
p1s.fix: State the construction once where the predictors are defined - each expression predictor is the concept mean minus the line's own mean over a seeded random 2,500-gene background, divided by its SD over the same background - and extend the 'not transcriptome-wide' caveat from the signature to all expr:: rows. Correct 'a log2(TPM+1) mean over the Reactome double-strand-break-response set' to the standardised form.

what_i_read: git history of research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py and research/modalities/depmap_sarcoma_dependency.py at the pin (git log --full-history, git log -S, per-commit git show of the four part-D bars and the three section-1 cuts)

p2s.summary: Part C's 'fraction dependent' column is computed over a different population from the one the sentence describes. Nothing moves, because the sarcoma-pool figure is higher, but the column and the sentence are about different sets of lines.
p2s.evidence: SS4: 'the axis sits at the floor in both groups - mean -1.340 across the sarcoma pool, 99.2-100 % of lines "dependent" on ATR and CHEK1'. The field is emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_c_coordinated_dependency.per_gene.<gene>.frac_dependent_panel_wide, computed in emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 2489-2491 as `sum(1 for v in vals[g].values() if v < DEPENDENT_THRESHOLD) / max(1, len(vals[g]))` over all 1,178 CRISPR lines, not over the 91-line sarcoma pool. SS1's definition ('the fraction of lines with a CRISPR gene effect below -0.5') names no population either. The sarcoma-pool version is a different field, #part_c...knockout_instrument_with_matched_comparator.frac_lines_dependent_on_axis_sarcoma_pool: 1.0.

p2s.summary: No familywise level is stated anywhere and no multiplicity control is applied, while the document prints roughly 120 test statistics. The paper discloses the missing intervals and not the missing correction.
p2s.evidence: Part B: 12 concepts x 4 contrasts x 2 readable platforms; part C: 7 genes x 2 comparators plus the joint z contrast; part D: 10 predictors x 7 drugs, all with t values. SS5 says 'No interval is computed anywhere in this analysis' but nothing says no correction is applied. It matters least where the decision rules are magnitude-based (all of them are) and most where the prose leans on t: SS3.4's 'The only sets that move are again the non-DDR ones - MYC targets +0.084 (t 3.34), oxphos +0.113 (t 5.92), adipogenesis +0.047 (t 2.11)'. Adipogenesis fails the paper's own Delta > 0.2 cut and, at t 2.114 on df 6.9 (per_platform GSE24369 contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma), is p ~ 0.073 uncorrected - not significant at any conventional level, let alone across 12 concepts. 'Move' is used with a criterion the document never defines.

p2s.summary: The group difference the headline imports is computed against an unmatched, any-lineage comparator - the same comparator SS4 identifies as a defect and replaces for the CRISPR readout - and the paper does not say so. No matched-comparator drug contrast exists in any artifact.
p2s.evidence: Headline: paclitaxel Delta -0.526 (t -3.08), ceralasertib -0.491, berzosertib -0.423, olaparib -1.016, talazoparib -2.065 - all verified exactly against fet-ddr-axis-scan.json#atr_inhibitor_sensitivity_gdsc.by_drug.*.welch_line_median_corrected. Those same blocks carry `n_FET: 57` against `n_comparator: 1124` (azd6738), i.e. non-FET lines of ANY lineage. SS4 calls that 'the old comparator of 1,123 non-FET lines of any lineage' and replaces it with 71 matched sarcoma lines. So 'FET-rearranged lines are broadly drug-sensitive' is, on this comparator, indistinguishable from a lineage statement. The by_drug block holds no sarcoma-matched contrast, and rerunning it from the committed cache (part_c.groups.FET_sarcoma_only vs matched_sarcoma_FET_negative, intersected with the drug residuals) leaves only n = 6 vs 27, too small to settle.

p2s.summary: SS5's standard-error yardstick is taken at the wrong n and for the wrong correlation coefficient, both in the direction of understating how small the passing margin is.
p2s.evidence: 'At n ~ 700 the standard error on a single rho is ~ 0.038' is then applied to the passing row's margin, whose rho is at n = 597 and 565 (1/sqrt(n-3) = 0.0410 and 0.0422). The coefficients are Spearman, not Pearson - emc_atr_vulnerability.py `_spearman` at line 371, used at line 2846 - and Spearman's asymptotic SE is about 1.06/sqrt(n-3). Both corrections make the margin smaller than 0.41 SE, so the hedge 'passes on a margin this document cannot distinguish from zero' is if anything understated. Reporting only.

objections_i_raised_and_the_paper_alread: '-0.164 and -0.171 are dependent correlations on the same 704 lines, so the SE of a single rho is the wrong yardstick for their difference.' Refuted: Steiger's test computed from the committed cache gives rho(replication_stress, proliferation_MYC) = +0.495 and an SE of the difference of 0.0381 (azd6738) and 0.0404 (ve-822), against 0.0378 and 0.0391 for a single rho. The paper's 0.038 is right to two decimals and its 'not distinguishable' is right (Z = 0.24 and 0.16).

'The part-B t values might be computed over genes rather than samples, which would be pseudo-replication at n = 20,629 probes.' Refuted: the committed contrast blocks carry df of 6.3-15.8 on 10-vs-6 and 6-vs-29 sample groups, consistent with a Welch test over samples.

'The pooled part-B contrast might average GSE4303 and GSE24369, contradicting SS6.1's claim that GSE4303 alone feeds the predicates.' Refuted: every entry of pooled_raw_contrast carries `n_platforms: 1`, and `platforms_with_a_readable_EMC_vs_comparator_contrast` is the single element GSE4303-GPL3290.

'The three SS1 cuts may have moved after the numbers landed.' Refuted: `bool(ddr_up_adj) and len(ctrl_up) <= 1`, the `> 0.2` elevated cut and `DEPENDENT_THRESHOLD = -0.5` are byte-identical at every commit touching either module in the ancestry of the pin.

'The SS1 rank key may be a post-hoc description of what happened.' Refuted: it matches `_rank_key` at emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 2151-2154 exactly - (-len(readable_platforms), -n_EMC, -max_scored_concepts_on_one_platform, series) - and GSE4303 wins on the EMC tiebreak 10 vs 6 as SS1 states.

'Whether +0.157 and +0.173 are distinguishable may be measurable after all, which would weaken the WEE1 point.' Partly: Steiger on the committed cache gives berzosertib vs adavosertib Z = 0.73 (not distinguishable, as the paper says) but ceralasertib vs adavosertib Z = 2.18, nominally distinguishable. One drug of two, uncorrected - not enough to disturb 'no bar in this analysis separates ATR from a neighbouring checkpoint kinase', which the paper states honestly.

'The specificity column is a signed mean over two opposite-sign controls, so a near-zero value records cancellation.' The paper raises this itself, prints every per-drug value, and states that its own proliferation control passes the bar as a result.

'GSE24369's comparator is 59 % LGFMS, another FET fusion, where the hypothesis predicts no difference - so a null there adds nothing.' The paper labels the arm as FET, reports the FET-arm-alone contrast separately, and the artifact's unreported non-FET-only arm (contrast_EMC_vs_NONFET_comparators, 6 desmoid + 6 fibrosarcoma) is null on every DDR concept too (|Delta| <= 0.049), so nothing is hidden that would change the reading.

'Part C is a null at n = 20 vs 71 with no power statement.' The paper does not claim a bound from it: it grades the part INSTRUMENT_STILL_BLIND and states in terms that it 'must not be quoted as evidence against the hypothesis ... It cannot refute it', and SS6.1 counts it as an absent reading rather than a null.
notes: Every printed statistic I checked reproduces exactly against the committed artifacts: part D's 70 correlations (I re-derived the Spearman rho and n for every published row from emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json and matched the artifact to four decimals), part C's six per-gene rows and the coordination block, part B's two contrast tables on both platforms, and the five imported group-difference deltas from fet-ddr-axis-scan.json. The arithmetic is sound and the decision rules are effect-size based rather than p-based, which is the right choice at these n and which makes the absent multiplicity control largely harmless. What my lens found is not in the numbers but in two statements about what the instruments can bound. The pre-registration claim is the serious one: the fourth part-D bar exists because of a prior run's numbers, the module says so in its own words, and the multiplier chosen with those numbers visible is what makes the count '1 of 4' rather than '0 of 4' - and the git-history defence SS1 offers cannot verify pre-registration because the module's first commit already postdates the runs its comments cite. The second is that the paper tells the reader twice, incompatibly, whether part B demonstrates absence; the minimum detectable effect it says was never computed is SE = |delta|/|t| on numbers the artifact already carries, and it says the proliferation-adjusted read is powered against the paper's own 0.2 cut on every concept on both series. Two further things the paper flags as missing turn out to be computable at $0 from the committed inputs cache, and both go the paper's way: the pan-essential dependency null is null (RPL5 +0.037, PLK1 +0.008 against the ATR axis's +0.212), and the per-gene decomposition shows the passing row is carried by ATR and ATRIP rather than by the three-gene module the text credits.
